question: Summarize the purpose of domain analysis in one sentence.
gt: To determine the domain’s concepts, stakeholders, constraints, and language so feasibility and scope can be judged.

question: Summarize how domain models and behavioral models relate in this lecture.
gt: Domain models define structure; behavioral models show how those relationships change over time (how the system behaves).

question: State why multiplicities on associations are important in domain models.
gt: They constrain the number of participating entities and clarify cardinality for correctness.

question: Explain the difference between association, aggregation, and composition as presented.
gt: Association = generic link; aggregation = whole-part (looser); composition = whole-part with strong lifetime dependency.

question: In one sentence, explain the role of include versus extend between use cases.
gt: Include extracts mandatory shared behavior; extend conditionally adds optional behavior to a base use case.

question: Give the template for user stories used in agile per the lecture.
gt: As a <type of user>, I want <some goal> so that <some reason>.

question: Describe what an epic story is and how it is handled.
gt: A large, high-level story that spans more than one iteration and must be decomposed into smaller user stories.

question: Provide two examples of non-functional requirements mentioned.
gt: Security (e.g., encrypt card numbers and PINs), performance (respond within 5 seconds), reliability, scalability, usability.

question: State the main purpose of a Software Requirements Specification in this lecture.
gt: To integrate functional and non-functional requirements (plus domain analysis) into a signed-off contract and basis for estimates.

question: According to the estimation precision slide, why are early cost/schedule estimates highly uncertain?
gt: Because at feasibility/requirements stages estimation error can be off by up to ~4x, improving only as the project advances.
